text: dsh-llm-xai-oauth 是面向 DSH 的 xAI/Grok 模型提供方，通过设备码 OAuth 使用 SuperGrok 或 X Premium 订阅，并将 xai 路由注册到 LLM 服务。插件可查找已有的本机 Grok 登录，按需完成登录和令牌刷新，适用于 TUI、Web 与 headless 配置；适配器支持流式文本、工具调用、图片输入、模型目录读取和上下文预算处理。另提供登录、状态、刷新及独立守护进程命令，方便在 DSH 未运行时维持访问令牌。需要 SuperGrok/X Premium 账号，不需要 xAI API key；提示和生成请求会发送到 Grok 服务端。

dsh-llm-xai-oauth connects DSH to Grok using OAuth for a SuperGrok or X Premium subscription. It registers the xai route and refreshes tokens. The adapter supports streaming, tools, images, model lookup, and context budgeting; its CLI offers login and a refresh daemon. No xAI API key is needed.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth 的功能「Grok 模型路由」：把 xAI OAuth 适配器注册为 DSH 的 xai 提供方，支持读取模型列表并通过流式请求生成回复。可用于 DSH 的模型选择与默认模型配置。
dsh-llm-xai-oauth 的功能「订阅 OAuth 登录与续期」：启动时查找可复用的本机 Grok 凭据，缺少时提供设备码登录；CLI 可查看令牌状态、手动刷新，或运行独立守护进程定期续期。
dsh-llm-xai-oauth 的功能「流式请求与上下文预算」：将 Grok 返回的事件流转换为 DSH 的文本、推理和工具调用内容；根据上下文窗口估算请求余量，在需要时报告溢出或调整生成上限。
dsh-llm-xai-oauth 使用 SuperGrok/X Premium 订阅的 OAuth 凭据，不需要 xAI API key；模型提示与请求会携带 OAuth 访问令牌发送至 cli-chat-proxy.grok.com。

You already pay for SuperGrok / X Premium. This plugin puts that subscription
into DeepSeek Harness as a live `xai` route: `grok-4.7`, device-code login,
token refresh that does not depend on a TUI being open. No xAI API key.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · dsh-llm-xai-oauth：Works in **headless**, **web**, and any terminal profile. The SSH TUI
[dsh-ssh-tui](https://github.com/cyjyyd/dsh-ssh-tui) can sit on top; it is not
required.

Install from **npm** (do not use the GitHub source unless you are developing):

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · dsh-llm-xai-oauth：```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-llm-xai-oauth@latest
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth login
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth daemon --install
dsh --profile headless --provider xai --model grok-4.7

Swap `headless` for `web` or `tui`. **Updates must use `@latest`.** A bare
`add dsh-llm-xai-oauth` keeps whatever version pnpm already pinned.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Three facts that matter：1. **This is subscription OAuth, not an API key.** After install, dsh talks to `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com` with the access token in `~/.grok-bridge/auth.json`.
2. **The access token lasts about an hour.** While dsh is running, the plugin refreshes five minutes before expiry and again on HTTP 401. If dsh is not running, that refresh does not happen.
3. **So you need a refresher that is not the dsh process.** Use `dsh-llm-xai-oauth daemon`. Do not expect the TUI or a headless one-shot to keep the token alive overnight.
dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Three facts that matter：`/usage` returning 401, then chat also 401, almost always means: the token expired and nothing was refreshing it.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Setup in five minutes：You need Node.js ≥ 22.19 and a DeepSeek Harness CLI (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`).
Verified on `0.1.5-rc.1` through `0.1.5-rc.3`, on `0.1.7-rc.1` and `0.1.7-rc.2`, on `0.2.0-rc.1` and `0.2.0-rc.2`, and on `0.2.1-rc.2`
through `0.2.1-rc.5` — the line the Windows and macOS desktop builds ship. `0.1.2`, the `0.1.6` alphas and the `0.2.x` alphas are not
supported. See the [compatibility audit](https://github.com/cyjyyd/dsh-llm-xai-oauth/blob/main/docs/compatibility-audit-0.2.1-rc.5.md) for the evidence behind that list.

dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-llm-xai-oauth@latest
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-llm-xai-oauth@latest
dsh plugin --profile tui add dsh-llm-xai-oauth@latest
```

section: 2. Log in once (from a machine that can open a browser)

text:
dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · force a new device-code even when a token already exists:：npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth login --force
```

The CLI prints a URL and a user code. Authorize SuperGrok / X Premium in the browser. On success it writes:

- token: `~/.grok-bridge/auth.json` (`0600`)
- dsh default model: `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` `agent-default-model` → `xai` / `grok-4.7`  
  (if that section is already `xai`, your grok model and effort are left alone)

Headless / CI hosts without a TTY skip the prompt. Set `DSH_XAI_OAUTH_NO_LOGIN=1` to skip it even on a TTY.

text: dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Windows and the desktop app: visual first-run guide：The guide stays up until the page has painted the final state and acknowledged it (5 s cap), so a successful authorization is always visible before the port closes. If the browser cannot be launched — a spawn failure or a blocked default browser — the button says so inline and the authorization URL is announced on stderr, instead of reporting a success that never happened.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Windows and the desktop app: visual first-run guide：The page is served from `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port under a random 128-bit path, so no other local process can read the pending code. It pulls in no external asset and needs no network beyond the xAI endpoints.

GROK_BRIDGE_NO_BROWSER=1 npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth login   # never launch a browser
```

text:
dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 3. Keep the token fresh (this is not dsh)：Access tokens are short. A TUI, headless job, or cron that starts after expiry will read a dead token; `/usage` and chat then 401.

**Recommended: a user systemd unit**

```bash
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth daemon --install
```

That writes `~/.config/systemd/user/dsh-llm-xai-oauth.service` and `enable --now`. The process re-reads `auth.json` about once a minute and refreshes five minutes before expiry. dsh does not need to be running.

No systemd, or you do not want a user unit:

```bash
section: 3. Keep the token fresh (this is not dsh)

text: dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · foreground：npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth daemon

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · or cron every 20 minutes (no-op while the token is still valid)：*/20 * * * * npx --yes dsh-llm-xai-oauth refresh >/tmp/dsh-xai-refresh.log 2>&1
```

Remove the user unit:

```bash
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth daemon --uninstall
```

Refresh once by hand:

```bash
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth refresh
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth refresh --force
```
section: or cron every 20 minutes (no-op while the token is still valid)

text:
dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 4. Run one SuperGrok turn：```bash
grep -A3 agent-default-model ~/.dsh/settings.yaml

dsh --profile tui --provider xai --model grok-4.7
dsh --profile headless "Reply with exactly: xai-harness-ok. Do not use tools."

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 4. Run one SuperGrok turn：In [dsh-ssh-tui](https://github.com/cyjyyd/dsh-ssh-tui): `/model` picks Grok; `/usage` reads the SuperGrok weekly remaining quota. The TUI now refreshes a due token before `/usage`, and on 401 it force-refreshes once and retries. **That covers “I opened the TUI just as the token expired”. It does not cover “the machine slept overnight with no refresher”.** Step 3 is that refresher.
dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Switching models later：```yaml

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml：agent-default-model:
  provider: xai
  model: grok-4.7
  reasoningEffort: high
```

Or pass `--provider` / `--model`, or use `/model` in the TUI. At startup the plugin calls `GET {baseURL}/models` with the current token; `/model` prefers that live catalog (currently `grok-4.7` with xhigh, `grok-4.5` up to high). The static fallback still lists `grok-4.3`.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml：| Model | Context | Output cap | Reasoning efforts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grok-4.7` | 500K | 64K | off / low / medium / high / xhigh |
| `grok-4.5` | 500K | 64K | off / low / medium / high |
| `grok-4.3` | 1M | 30K | off / low / medium / high |

`max` in a DeepSeek-style picker maps to `xhigh`.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml：Optional plugin settings are `baseURL`, `reasoningEffort`, `models`, and the retry / idle timeout. On `0.1.5` they live under `llm-xai-oauth:` in `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`. On `0.1.7` they live in the profile patch and `0.1.7` imports that file once, on its first start. Either way a change reaches the next request without a restart.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml：Long SuperGrok chats can fill the 500K window and then 400 with a generic `INVALID_REQUEST` because `max_tokens` no longer fits. From 0.1.3 the adapter projects the next prompt from the last usage sample and, when remaining context cannot hold the requested completion, throws `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` so harness overflow compaction can retry. Compaction / title calls still go through, with `max_tokens` clamped to the remainder.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 401 / expiry：```bash
npx dsh-llm-xai-oauth status
ls -l ~/.grok-bridge/auth.json
systemctl --user status dsh-llm-xai-oauth.service
journalctl --user -u dsh-llm-xai-oauth.service -n 50

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 401 / expiry：| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/usage` or chat HTTP 401 | access token expired, nothing refreshed it | `refresh --force`, then install the daemon |
| chat HTTP 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` on a long session | remaining context < `max_tokens`; older plugin versions did not trip compaction | update to 0.1.3+; `/compact` if a turn already failed |
| status says `no refresh_token` | truncated file / not an OAuth login | `login --force` |
| dump-config has no `llm-xai-oauth` | plugin is not in this profile | repeat step 1 |
| token exists but dsh still uses DeepSeek | `agent-default-model` is not `xai` | `/model`, or edit settings.yaml |
| `daemon --install` fails | no user systemd / linger | use cron, or `loginctl enable-linger $USER` |

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 401 / expiry：`HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` apply to login, refresh, and chat.

Override client / endpoints only when xAI changes them:

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · 401 / expiry：| Env | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `GROK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | `b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828` |
| `GROK_OAUTH_SCOPE` | `openid profile email offline_access grok-cli:access api:access` |
| `GROK_OAUTH_BASE` | `https://auth.x.ai` |
| `GROK_UPSTREAM_BASE` | `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1` |
| `DSH_XAI_OAUTH_NO_LOGIN` | skip the startup device-code prompt |
| `GROK_BRIDGE_NO_BROWSER` | print the URL instead of opening a browser |

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · What it is not：- Not an xAI API-key provider. Metered `api.x.ai` stays on the generic catalog.
- Not a Codex / Claude / Copilot aggregator.
- Not a Web “one-click login” settings card, and no OAuth redirect port is opened. Device authorization stays the mechanism; the Windows guide merely renders that code in a browser page for hosts without a console.
- Does not `registerConfigurableProviders('xai')`; `llm-pi-ai` already owns that catalog key. This package owns the **live adapter route**.

dsh-llm-xai-oauth README · Layout：```text
src/index.ts        Cordis plugin: search / login / register the xai route
src/cli.ts          login / status / refresh / daemon
src/bootstrap.ts    local token search, device login, dsh default model
src/onboarding.ts   browser guide for the first-run device login (Windows)
